title: Flood Advisory
location: Bergen, NJ; Essex, NJ; Hudson, NJ; Passaic, NJ; Orange, NY; Putnam, NY; Rockland, NY; Westchester, NY

details.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast New Jersey, including the following
counties, Bergen, Essex, Hudson and Passaic and southeast New
York, including the following counties, Orange, Putnam, Rockland
and Westchester.

* WHEN...Until 130 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1019 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Paterson, Passaic, Wayne, Bloomfield, Hackensack, New City,
Newburgh, Bergenfield, Paramus, Ossining, Ridgewood,
Peekskill, Lyndhurst, Monsey, Rutherford, Nanuet, Ramsey,
Ringwood, Haverstraw and Pompton Lakes.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

details.description:

Central Nevada today, with historically high atmospheric moisture
content. The strongest showers and thunderstorms today will produce
intense rainfall rates, resulting in the potential of flash flooding.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Most of Northern and Central Nevada.

* WHEN...From 11 AM PDT this morning until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The strongest showers and thunderstorms today will produce
rainfall rates of around one and one quarter of an inch per
hour, resulting in the potential of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

details.instruction:

title: Flood Warning
location: Dimmit, TX

details.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 31.0 feet, The Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a
mile and a half wide south and west of Crystal City. Farm to
Market 190 is flooded over a mile near the Nueces River and the
bridge floor is flooded. Livestock should be moved from the flood
plain. Upstream, Highway 85 becomes impassable as routed water
spills into Soldier Slough and over the highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 29.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 8:30 AM CDT Tuesday was 30.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 30.3
feet just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
30.2 feet on 07/04/2002.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight by 300 AM CDT.

title: Rip Current Statement
location: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

details.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8
to 11 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM this afternoon to
6 AM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening swimming
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
details.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

title: Heat Advisory
location: Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon; Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon; Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon; Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Washington; Yakima Valley; Lower Columbia Basin of Washington; Foothills of the Blue Mountains of Washington

details.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures up to 100 to 103 degrees
expected, with 101 to 105 degrees in the Columbia Basin. This will
pose a moderate to major risk of heat-related illness.

* WHERE...Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon and Washington,
Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon and Washington, Foothills of the
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon, Yakima Valley, and Foothills of
the Blue Mountains of Washington.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 9 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heat will begin today, with widespread
moderate and locally major HeatRisk.

Wednesday looks to be the hottest day, with Major HeatRisk across
the Columbia Basin, Yakima Valley and portions of the Gorge and Blue
Mountain Foothills.

Thursday will also see widespread moderate HeatRisk and locally
major HeatRisk, mainly across the Columbia Basin.

Smoke from area wildfires could end up affecting how hot
temperatures get.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit 211info.org for Oregon or
wa211.org for Washington anytime.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Sussex, NJ; Warren, NJ

details.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Sussex County in northwestern New Jersey...
Northern Warren County in northwestern New Jersey...

* Until 100 PM EDT.

* At 849 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2.5 inches in
1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
drainage and low lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Newton, Blairstown, Franklin, Ogdensburg, Hope, Andover,
Greendell, Allamuchy-Panther Valley, Great Meadows-Vienna, Lake
Mohawk, Columbia and Portland.

This includes Interstate 80 in New Jersey between mile markers 3 and
18.
details.instruction:
Turn around...don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most
flood deaths occur in vehicles.

details.description:
A few isolated thunderstorms have developed both to the northeast
and southwest of Sanak Island this morning. These storms have had
a history of producing frequent lightning. Mariners can expect
erratic and gusty winds and locally higher waves as well as
frequent lightning strikes if around these storms. Additional
thunderstorms may develop over these zones through this morning.
However, thunderstorms are generally moving east-southeast and
should exit out of the two zones toward the Shumagin Islands and
south by later this morning.
